name: Memorization and Meditation (Puritan Practice)

objectives.text: Recite short key verses from memory such as Genesis 1:1 and John 3:16
Use repetition, motions, or song to learn a verse word for word until it can be said without help
Recite from memory a verse that tells of God's care in times of fear such as Psalm 56:3 or Isaiah 41:10
State the book, chapter, and verse reference together with each memorized verse
Recite longer passages from memory such as Psalm 23 or the Beatitudes
Recite catechism answers from memory along with a supporting proof text
Explain the meaning of a memorized verse in your own words
Explain from Psalm 119 and Deuteronomy 6 why God commands His people to store His Word in their hearts
Describe how Jesus answered each temptation in the wilderness by quoting Scripture
Select a memorized verse that addresses a specific temptation and explain how its truth answers that temptation
Distinguish between memorizing the words of Scripture and meditating on them using Psalm 1 and Joshua 1
Meditate on a memorized passage by working through it phrase by phrase and writing a question and observation for each phrase
Explain the Puritan picture of meditation as chewing on the Word using writers such as Thomas Watson or Richard Baxter
Connect a memorized verse to other passages that teach the same doctrine
Examine the context of a commonly memorized verse such as Jeremiah 29:11 or Philippians 4:13 to show how it is rightly and wrongly applied
Contrast biblical meditation, which fills the mind with God's Word, with forms of meditation that seek to empty the mind
Construct a system for reviewing and retaining memorized Scripture over months and years
Explain how the Reformed tradition relates reading, memorizing, and meditating on Scripture to the means of grace and to prayer
Evaluate from Scripture and Puritan writings the role meditation plays in resisting sin and cultivating delight in God
Compose a written meditation on a passage that moves from its meaning to its doctrine to its practical implications
Defend from Scripture the practice of hiding God's Word in the heart as part of the believer's spiritual armor, answering common objections to memorization

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (reciting key verses, longer passages, explaining meaning, applying to temptation, phrase-by-phrase meditation, Puritan chewing image, connecting doctrine, context checking, review system, written meditation, defense). Reframed the comfort verse objective from a feeling to recall of verses about God's care. Dropped the handwriting copy filler. Added reference recall, catechism memorization with proof texts, the biblical basis for storing the Word, Christ's use of Scripture in temptation, contrast with empty-mind meditation, and meditation's place among the means of grace. Added verse-level scripture and confession anchors where the doctrine is stated.
